subject: Re: Service degradation — p95/p99 latency & 5xx surge (OpalCare)
messages:
From: Daniel Reed <daniel.reed@opalcare.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@opalcare.com>, Evelyn Wu <evelyn.wu@opalcare.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden latency & 5xx spike — production impact

Marissa —

We're seeing a severe degradation on our production traffic to the Redwood hosted API starting around 07:55 PST. p95 has jumped from ~220ms to ~3.1s and p99 is above 6s. We're also seeing a surge in 5xx errors (~4.3% over the last 20 minutes). This is impacting our user flows (document ingestion and live assist).

Attached: opalcare_latency_screenshot.png for dashboard view.

Can you please confirm what you can run right now and whether we should fail open to our cached responses? We have a health check window in 30m and procurement is watching SLA credits.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director of Engineering
OpalCare
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 08:46:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency & 5xx spike — production impact

Thanks for flagging, Daniel — we're on it.

Quick asks while we triage:
- Can you share a sample request id (one or two) that resulted in a 5xx?
- Are these spikes isolated to a subset of routes/models or across all endpoints?

I've looped in Rishi and Monica from SRE/CS. We'll get a dedicated bridge and proposed mitigations within 20m.

Marissa Cole

marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 08:55:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency & 5xx spike — preliminary triage

On Fri, Dec 18, 2026 at 08:46 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for flagging, Daniel — we're on it.

Prelim triage from the runtime side: we see a correlated increase in GPU memory allocator churn on several hosted nodes serving OpalCare's traffic. There are frequent kernel eviction/realloc events and an uptick in KV cache memory pressure for long-session conversations. This pattern looks like fragmentation leading to OOMs and per-request stalls — matches p99 spikes and 5xxs.

I'm pulling a heap dump and runtime logs now (will attach runtime_heapdump_20261218.log once sanitized). Short term mitigation options:
- Route OpalCare to our less-loaded GPU pool (can do within ~10-15m, potential cost impact)
- Temporarily switch their route to the quantized-compact model variant (reduces mem footprint, slightly different quality)
- Apply a rate limiter on long sessions to release KV cache sooner

I'll coordinate with Neha to scope an allocator patch, but that's a longer timeline.

-Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Reed <daniel.reed@opalcare.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Wu <evelyn.wu@opalcare.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency & 5xx spike — proposed immediate mitigations

Daniel —

Thanks. Based on engineering's recommendation, here are immediate steps we propose (can execute after your sign-off):
1) Route OpalCare traffic to a less-utilized GPU pool (estimated cut in p99 within 10-20m)
2) Swap your production route to quantized-compact model variant (quality impact: small on very long context prompts)
3) Enforce a temporary per-session KV timeout (drop idle/concluded sessions after 60s of inactivity)
4) Apply a circuit-breaker to fail fast for requests exceeding 7s to reduce tail amplification

Expected timeline: 10-30m for routing + model swap; 1-2 hours for KV timeout + circuit breaker rollout. We'll monitor and share dashboards continuously.

Please reply "approve" if you'd like us to proceed now. If you'd prefer a maintenance window, we can schedule immediate phased changes.

Marissa

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 14:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Incident update & short-term remediation completed

Status update (post-mitigation):
- 12/18 09:15 PST: Routed OpalCare traffic to lower-utilization GPU pool (p99 dropped from ~6s to ~650ms)
- 12/18 09:22 PST: Swapped OpalCare route to quantized-compact variant (minor quality delta observed on extreme long-turn prompts)
- 12/18 10:00 PST: Applied per-session KV timeout and circuit-breaker to reduce tail amplification

Root cause (engineering summary): repeated small allocations in the runtime allocator combined with long-lived KV caches caused fragmentation on specific GPU node kernels; combined with a transient spike in long-context sessions this produced soft OOMs and eviction stalls. We're scheduling an allocator improvement + defragmentation routine in the runtime for next week.

Attachments: runtime_heapdump_20261218.log, mitigation_checklist_v2.pdf

Next steps:
- Rishi to ship allocator patch and small runtime defrag job (ETA 2026-12-25)
- Postmortem + RCA to be published by 2026-12-23
- Lauren: we'll provide a suggested SLA credit and a short-term dedicated pool option for OpalCare if requested

-Neha Kapoor
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
